click.tech: Moves the mouse to the coordinates then clicks through the operating system's input API (macOS: CGEvent; Windows: SendInput, real pixel coordinates so it is correct at 125 % / 150 %).
click.accuracy: Pixel-exact – as long as the window does not move. The point is saved relative to the region + anchor, so a resized window still follows the right button if the anchor is on the right edge.
click.speed: Instant; with Human-like on, the mouse follows a curve and takes a few hundred ms longer.
good: A window pinned with the Window node
Games / canvas with no text or elements to find
avoid: A button that moves with the content → [[node:clickText]] or [[node:clickElement]]
A public web page → [[node:webClick]]
tips: Add points quickly: open the overlay, move the mouse to the button, press F6.
Clicking several times: set the count + the gap between clicks in the node itself, no loop needed.

When several apps easily cover each other: turn on *Only in window* (`onlyInWindow` + app / title) – if the window is closed or not in front, the node reports `window_mismatch` and has not clicked / typed anything; add a [[node:window]] node first to bring it to the front.
fields: **Point** – where to click (coordinates + anchor relative to the window)
**Count** and **gap** – click several times in one node
**Human-like** – the mouse follows a curve, random delays

double.tech: Two consecutive clicks through the operating system's input API (like the Click node with count = 2), fast enough that the app treats it as a double-click.
double.accuracy: Pixel-exact like Click; an app slow to respond may miss the double-click if the machine is busy.
good: Open a file / folder, select a whole word
Maximise a window by double-clicking the title bar
avoid: A spot whose position changes with the content → switch to [[node:clickImage]] and click by image / text / element
A web box with its own button → [[node:webClick]] is steadier
tips: Double-click not working: try Click then Click again with a small gap, or press Enter to open the selected item.

When several apps easily cover each other: turn on *Only in window* (`onlyInWindow` + app / title) – if the window is closed or not in front, the node reports `window_mismatch` and has not clicked / typed anything; add a [[node:window]] node first to bring it to the front.
fields: **Point** – where to double-click (coordinates + anchor relative to the window)
**Human-like** – the mouse follows a curve to the point

hold.tech: Presses the mouse button, holds for exactly the number of milliseconds, then releases; it always releases, even if you press Stop midway.
hold.accuracy: Exact position; the hold time is off by a few tens of ms depending on how busy the machine is.
hold.speed: Exactly the hold time you set.
good: A button that must be held to act (hold to confirm, hold to record)
Games that need the mouse held
avoid: Only one click needed → [[node:click]]
Dragging from one point to another → [[node:drag]]
tips: Set the hold time a little longer than the app requires.

When several apps easily cover each other: turn on *Only in window* (`onlyInWindow` + app / title) – if the window is closed or not in front, the node reports `window_mismatch` and has not clicked / typed anything; add a [[node:window]] node first to bring it to the front.

drag.tech: Moves the mouse to point A, presses and holds, moves to point B over the set duration, then releases (it always releases when stopped). It can start from where the mouse already is, or compute point B from an offset.
drag.accuracy: Pixel-exact if the window does not move; an app that checks drag events strictly needs a slightly longer drag time.
drag.speed: The drag time set in the node.
good: Drag a kanban card, drag a file into a folder
Drag a slider, highlight text
avoid: Dragging along a curve / through several points → [[node:path]]
A start point that moves → find it with [[node:clickImage]] and feed it into Drag via coordinate variables
tips: Drag not working: increase the drag time, or turn on Human-like so the mouse accelerates.
Dragging from where something was just found: use the option to start from where the previous node left the mouse.

When several apps easily cover each other: turn on *Only in window* (`onlyInWindow` + app / title) – if the window is closed or not in front, the node reports `window_mismatch` and has not clicked / typed anything; add a [[node:window]] node first to bring it to the front.
fields: **Start from where the mouse stopped** and **B is an offset**

path.tech: Holds the mouse button and drags one continuous stroke: through the points, or a ready-made circle / rectangle / star around a centre. The time is divided by each segment's length.
path.accuracy: Follows the set points / shape exactly; a drawing app that handles mouse events slowly may make the stroke rough – lengthen the draw time.
path.speed: The draw time set in the node.
good: Drawing apps, signatures, pattern-lock unlock
Dragging through several points in one stroke
avoid: Just a straight drag A → B → [[node:drag]]
tips: Preview the stroke on the overlay before running.
Turn on Human-like: each segment curves slightly, with speed-up / slow-down like a real hand.

When several apps easily cover each other: turn on *Only in window* (`onlyInWindow` + app / title) – if the window is closed or not in front, the node reports `window_mismatch` and has not clicked / typed anything; add a [[node:window]] node first to bring it to the front.
fields: **Join the last point back to the first**

scroll.tech: Sends mouse-wheel events (notch count, up / down / left / right) at the set point or where the mouse is.
scroll.accuracy: How many pixels one notch scrolls is decided by the app and the OS – it does not scroll an exact fixed number of lines.
good: See more content, a feed, a long list
Scroll a little at a time, then check with Wait / Find
avoid: Scrolling inside a web page frame → [[node:webScroll]] is more precise
Need to scroll until something appears → put Scroll in a loop with [[node:waitImage]]
tips: Scroll not working: put the point on the area to scroll so the mouse stands over that frame.

When several apps easily cover each other: turn on *Only in window* (`onlyInWindow` + app / title) – if the window is closed or not in front, the node reports `window_mismatch` and has not clicked / typed anything; add a [[node:window]] node first to bring it to the front.

type.tech: Two ways to enter text: type key by key, or paste through the clipboard and restore the old text. The default picks automatically: Windows without Human-like pastes, otherwise it types keys.
type.accuracy: Typing keys is exact with unaccented text; a background Vietnamese input method (UniKey, EVKey…) can garble accented text when typing keys – choose Paste or turn the input method off.
type.speed: Paste is almost instant; typing depends on the character count, slower with Human-like on (uneven rhythm, occasionally mistyping then deleting).
good: Fill forms, search boxes, messages (after a Click into the field)
Enter a value from a variable, e.g. {{n3.output.text}}
avoid: A web field with a clear selector → [[node:webType]]
A field that blocks pasting – do not choose Paste
tips: To type a literal {{ write \{{.
Vietnamese text garbled: switch the input method to Paste.
Need Enter after typing: add a [[node:key]] node.

When several apps easily cover each other: turn on *Only in window* (`onlyInWindow` + app / title) – if the window is closed or not in front, the node reports `window_mismatch` and has not clicked / typed anything; add a [[node:window]] node first to bring it to the front.

key.tech: Presses a key or combination through the operating system's input API. Chord mode holds them together (Ctrl+C); sequence mode holds the modifier keys then presses the others one by one.
key.accuracy: Exact key; keys only take effect on the focused window – check the window first with the Window node.
good: Enter to send, Tab to move between fields, Esc to close
Copy / paste, switch tab, open the machine's find box
avoid: Typing a whole passage → [[node:type]]
Keys for a web page whose window may lose focus → [[node:webKey]]
tips: Cmd (macOS) and Ctrl (Windows) differ: a script meant for both should be checked on each machine.
Key names follow robotgo: enter, tab, esc, f5, a…

When several apps easily cover each other: turn on *Only in window* (`onlyInWindow` + app / title) – if the window is closed or not in front, the node reports `window_mismatch` and has not clicked / typed anything; add a [[node:window]] node first to bring it to the front.

wait.tech: Just waits the exact number of milliseconds (Stop and pause still take effect immediately mid-wait).
wait.accuracy: Exactly the set time; it does not know whether the page / app is ready.
wait.speed: The set time – easy to wait too long or too little.
good: A short pause between two actions
No image, text or element to wait for
avoid: Waiting for a page to finish loading → [[node:waitScreen]] or [[node:waitImage]]
Waiting until a set time → [[node:waitUntil]]
tips: Every node has a *wait after* field – put a short pause there instead of adding a node.

waitPixel.tech: Reads the colour of one screen point each round and compares each RGB channel to the wanted colour (with a tolerance). It does not move the mouse. Needs Screen Recording permission on macOS.
waitPixel.accuracy: Exact at the chosen point; blur / colour-transition effects need a larger tolerance. A theme or window size change shifts the point.
waitPixel.speed: Faster than waiting for an image – it reads only one pixel.
good: A status light changing colour, a progress bar filling
A button turning from grey to green
avoid: Need to know where something with a shape appears → [[node:waitImage]]
Waiting for a page to finish loading → [[node:waitScreen]]
tips: On timeout the error reports the colour read at that point – use it to adjust the colour or tolerance.

waitScreen.tech: Captures an area each round and compares shrunken greyscale images: still (two consecutive captures nearly identical for long enough) or changed compared with the start. Needs Screen Recording permission on macOS.
waitScreen.accuracy: Good for pages / effects that change the whole area. A small spinner inside a large area changes less than 1 % – shrink the area or lower the threshold to 0.
waitScreen.speed: Finishes as soon as the area settles – no extra waiting like a fixed Wait.
good: After opening a page / clicking a button: wait for the page to finish loading
*Changed* mode right after a Click to know the app responded
avoid: You know exactly what will appear → [[node:waitImage]] is more reliable
An area with a running clock / ad never becomes still
tips: The timeout error includes the last difference % so you can adjust the threshold.

ocrRead.tech: Captures an area and reads all text with OCR (macOS: Vision; Windows: Tesseract with the Vietnamese pack), ordered top → bottom, left → right, dropping empty / duplicate lines. It re-reads until the area has text. Needs Screen Recording permission on macOS.
ocrRead.accuracy: Large, clear text on a plain background is read almost entirely right; small text / image backgrounds may get wrong accents or characters. For normal apps and normal Chrome, [[node:pageText]] reads the text verbatim.
ocrRead.speed: A few hundred ms to a few seconds depending on the area size – the smaller the area, the faster.
good: Read a status / amount in a game, image, remote desktop, image-based PDF, then branch with [[node:switch]]
Get a list of text lines to filter with [[node:textMatch]] / loop with [[node:forEach]]
avoid: Just need to know whether a text appears → [[node:waitImage]] (find by text)
Text next to a fixed label → [[node:elementRead]] (find = text)
A whole-screen area: mixed with other apps' text, slow to read
tips: Outline the area by node: choose *Area = by node* and point at a Window / Wait for image node so the area follows the window.
Comparing text in Switch is accent-sensitive – use the phrase with the fewest accents as the anchor.
fields: **Area** – script region / whole screen / chosen area / by node (like Screenshot)

waitUntil.tech: Waits until a set time by the machine clock or internet standard time (NTP). When far away it sleeps in steps of ≤ 1 s; near the time it waits in very short rounds.
waitUntil.accuracy: Off by a few ms. With standard time on, a wrong machine clock is still on time; if standard time cannot be fetched it uses machine time (output ntpOffsetMs = 0).
waitUntil.speed: Until the set time; Stop / pause take effect immediately while waiting.
good: Sale hunting, booking tickets exactly when they open
Daily jobs with a loop
avoid: Running a whole script on a schedule → the schedule in Settings
Waiting for something to finish → the other Wait nodes
tips: The time has already passed when the node is reached: choose to continue, wait until tomorrow, or report an error.
The machine must stay on and not sleep while waiting.
fields: **Set time** – HH:mm[:ss[.mmm]], optionally with a date

waitImage.tech: Matches a template image (captured by the app) against the screen each round, reporting the position and % match. Options: match by edges (tolerates light / dark theme changes), check the average colour to tell same-shaped buttons of different colours apart, and transparent areas of the template are not counted.
works: Native apps, games, canvas, remote desktop – where there is no text or element to read
Any web / app, as long as it is visible on screen
waitImage.accuracy: High with the same theme and the same zoom; a changed text size, zoom, DPI or partial covering lowers the match. Pick a moderate threshold and test on both themes.
waitImage.speed: Slower than reading elements, depending on the search area – shrink the search area to be faster. Needs Screen Recording permission on macOS.
good: Icons, logos, buttons without text
Games / canvas, apps whose elements cannot be read
avoid: A button with clear text and a theme that changes often → [[node:waitText]]
A signed-in web page or an app with a UI tree → [[node:waitElement]]
tips: Find by AI (the AI button in the Find by field): describe it in words and the AI looks at the search-area image. Slow, costs money and the search-area image leaves the machine (except for an on-machine AI) – use only when a template image / text / element cannot find it. Needs a provider in Settings → Ask AI.
Crop the template tightly, avoiding changing backgrounds and changing numbers / text (make that part transparent).
Not found: the error reports the highest match so you can adjust the threshold.
Need to click where it was found: use [[node:clickImage]] with “by node” pointing at this node.

waitText.tech: Reads the on-screen text with OCR (macOS: Vision; Windows: Tesseract with the Vietnamese pack) then looks for a line containing the wanted text. By default it ignores case, whitespace and accents.
works: Anything with text shown on screen: web, native apps, Electron
Not usable on games / canvas drawing very stylised text
waitText.accuracy: Steadier than images when the theme or zoom changes. Small, blurry text, patterned backgrounds or very stylised text may be misread – use a partial match instead of the whole line.
waitText.speed: Slower than reading elements because the whole area must be OCR'd; shrink the search area. Needs Screen Recording permission on macOS.
good: Wait for a “Success” message, a button name to appear
Buttons with a text label, a theme that changes often
avoid: Icons without text → [[node:waitImage]]
Need exactly accurate text, or the content of an input box → [[node:waitElement]]
tips: Several matching places: set “which occurrence” in reading order.
Need to tell accents apart (e.g. “ma” and “mà”): turn on exact-accent matching.
The text to find accepts {{variables}}.

waitElement.tech: Finds an element (button, field, text) through the operating system's UI tree (Windows: UI Automation; macOS: Accessibility) by text / label / role – no screenshot, no OCR.
works: Normal Chrome / Edge already signed in
Native and Electron apps with accessibility support
The window must be visible on screen (not minimised, not on another virtual display)
waitElement.accuracy: The highest: reads the exact text, the value of an input box, and icon-only buttons (if the app sets a label). An app that sets no accessibility labels or draws freely (games, canvas) has no elements.
waitElement.speed: Fast, independent of the area size. An element outside the viewport is scrolled into view automatically.
good: A signed-in web page when you do not want to use the app's own browser
An icon-only button that has an accessibility label
Read the content of a field / a price to use in a later node
avoid: A public page needing no sign-in → the Web nodes (the app's Chrome) are steadier
Games / canvas → [[node:waitImage]]
tips: Use the pick-element button in the inspector so the app suggests a durable way to find it.
A label with a changing part ("Messenger, 1 unread", "Inbox (3)") → write only the fixed part, no double quotes: aria=Messenger. Pasting aria-label=… from DevTools also works.
Waiting forever without finding it: check that the window is visible and that the app has Accessibility permission / runs with the same privileges.

clickImage.tech: Finds, then clicks the centre of what was found (plus an offset). Choose how to find right in the node: a template image, OCR text or an Accessibility / UI Automation element – or click where an earlier Wait node already found something.
works: Depends on the way to find: images for anything visible, text for anything with text, elements for apps with a UI tree
clickImage.accuracy: As per the chosen way to find (see the Wait for image / text / element pages). You can add an offset to click off-centre.
clickImage.speed: As per the chosen way to find; the click is instant once found.
good: A button that moves with the window or content
Click by a name shown on screen, e.g. “Sign in”
avoid: A button that always stays fixed → [[node:click]] is faster and simpler
Need to check whether something is visible and branch → Wait + If
tips: Not found goes out the Failed port – connect that port to an error-handling branch.
Element: the node waits for the frame to be still before clicking.
Sure it was already found by an earlier Wait node: choose “by node” to avoid searching again.
fields: **How to find** – image / text / element, or by a wait node

clickText.tech: It is Click by image / text / element with find = text: OCR (macOS: Vision; Windows: Tesseract Vietnamese) then clicks the line containing the text.
works: Web, native apps, Electron – anything with text shown on screen
clickText.accuracy: Steady when the theme / zoom changes; small text or busy backgrounds may be misread. It clicks the centre of the line containing the text – for a long line add an offset.
clickText.speed: Slower than elements because the search area is OCR'd; shrink the area to speed up.
good: Links, buttons with a text label
A button whose position changes with the layout
avoid: An icon without text → Click by image
Need absolute certainty about the text → Click by element
tips: Text appears in several places: set “which occurrence”.
The text to find accepts {{variables}}.

clickElement.tech: It is Click by image / text / element with find = element: finds it through the UI tree (Windows: UI Automation; macOS: Accessibility), waits for the frame to be still, then clicks with the real mouse.
works: Normal Chrome already signed in, native apps, Electron with accessibility support
clickElement.accuracy: The most exact when the app sets accessibility labels; with no labels it cannot be found.
good: An icon-only button that has a label
A signed-in web page
avoid: Games / canvas → Click by image
A public page → [[node:webClick]]
tips: Use the pick-element button so the app suggests a durable way to find it (it prefers labels over order).

findAll.tech: Like the Wait node but takes every match (image, text or element) and returns the count with a list of positions, in reading order (top → bottom, left → right). A template image gives at most 200 matches.
findAll.accuracy: As per the chosen way to find; a template image merges overlapping matches. Elements only include what is visible in the viewport.
findAll.speed: As per the chosen way to find; it looks again each cycle until the count is within the set range.
good: Click every “Add” / “Follow” button on a page in turn
Count results to branch
avoid: Only one match is needed → Wait for image / text / element
tips: Connect Find all → [[node:forEach]] (list = items) → Click at item.x / item.y.
On timeout without the minimum count → the Failed port, with the error reporting how many were found.
fields: **How to find** as in the Wait node

if.tech: Evaluates one condition (text / image / colour visible, compare values) then takes the true or false port. Screen-looking conditions use the same finding as the Wait nodes. With a wait time set, it re-checks regularly until true, and on timeout counts as false.
if.accuracy: As per the chosen condition (see the Wait for image / text pages). With a missing permission or a broken template image the node errors rather than taking the wrong port.
if.speed: A single check is instant; with a wait time it takes at most that long.
good: Optional work: if there is an ad close it, otherwise continue
Branch on a variable, an earlier node's result or what is on screen
avoid: Several states (three or more) → [[node:switch]] or [[node:switchScreen]]
Just waiting until something appears → a Wait node, no branching
tips: When it sees something the result has coordinates: connect [[node:clickImage]] with “by node” pointing at this If node.
Need to give the page time to appear before concluding “not there”: set a wait time instead of checking once.
fields: **Condition** – text / image / colour visible or compare values

switch.tech: Compares one value (usually a {{variable}}) in turn with each case: equals, contains (ignoring case) or regex. The first matching case takes its port; if none match the default port is used.
switch.accuracy: Exact for text / numbers already in the variable; it does not look at the screen.
good: Branch several ways on a run-time input or an earlier node's result
Classify text read: “Success” / “Error” / other
avoid: Only two branches → [[node:if]]
Deciding by what is on screen → [[node:switchScreen]]
tips: Case order matters: the first match wins.
Always connect the default port so the script does not stop unexpectedly.

switchScreen.tech: Captures the screen periodically, checks the cases in order (text / image / colour visible) and takes the port of the first true case. If no case is true by the timeout it takes the “none” port.
switchScreen.accuracy: Per condition (as on the Wait for image / text pages). The case checked first wins when two states show at once.
switchScreen.speed: Done as soon as a case is true; at most the wait time. Needs Screen Recording permission on macOS.
good: A page that can be in several states: sign-in / already in / popup
Wait for “one of several outcomes” instead of several Wait nodes
avoid: Deciding by a variable → [[node:switch]]
Only one state to check → [[node:if]]
tips: Put the case that must be handled first (e.g. a popup covering the screen) at the top.

forEach.tech: Repeats the loop body once for each item of a list: it loads the list on first entry, each entry takes the next item out the “item” port, and when finished goes out the “done” port. Source: lines of text, a JSON array, a .csv or .xlsx file (the first row is the column names).
forEach.accuracy: Reads the source data exactly; a broken file or a bad JSON array makes the node error and stops the script. An empty list goes out “done” at once.
forEach.speed: Only the time of the nodes in the loop body.
good: Do the same job for each Excel / CSV row
Click every spot Find all found, in turn
avoid: Repeating a fixed N times or until something appears → [[node:counter]] or the script's loop
tips: The end of the loop body must connect an edge back to this node.
Read the item: {{nX.output.item}} (text) or {{nX.output.item.column_name}} (a table row); {{nX.output.index}} counts from 1.
One script loop runs at most 10000 node executions – a very long list must be split.
The Preview button in the inspector shows the list that was read at once.

counter.tech: Counts passes through it within the loop: from pass 1 up to the limit it leaves the “Remaining” port, the next pass leaves the “Exhausted” port, then it counts again from 0.
counter.accuracy: Counts the exact number of passes through the node within one run loop.
good: Limit retries: button not found → Counter → scroll and search again; when exhausted, report an error
Do something every N times
avoid: Going through an existing list → [[node:forEach]]
tips: Place it on the loop's return path; connect the “Exhausted” port to an [[node:end]] that reports failure.

end.tech: Ends the run loop with a success or failure status plus a message (accepts {{variables}}). Failure stops the whole script and reports the error code “end”; success with loops remaining runs the next loop.
good: End an error branch with a clear message
End early once enough work is done
avoid: The end of a normal branch: no End node is needed, the script finishes by itself when the edges run out
tips: A success message is shown to the user when the run finishes and is in the output.
A failure message should state the cause with variables, e.g. “Button not found at row {{n2.output.index}}”.

setVar.tech: Sets or adds to a variable that later nodes read as {{vars.name}}. Assign accepts {{variables}}; add treats an unset value as 0. Variables reset at each run loop.
good: Keep a result for use in many later nodes
A counter / running total within a loop
avoid: Computing from numbers read → [[node:calc]]
Just using the result of the node right before → use {{nX.output.…}} directly
tips: The variable vanishes after each loop – to keep it longer write it to a file.
Adding a value that is text with a unit (e.g. “1,200 đ”): convert it to a number first with a text-processing node.

calc.tech: A hand-written calculator (Go and TS share a test suite): add, subtract, multiply, divide, comparisons, and / or / not, round / floor / ceil / abs / min / max. A text variable inserted becomes a string automatically.
calc.accuracy: Results are rounded to 10 decimal places. Dividing by 0 or a wrong type makes the node error and stops the script.
good: Add / compare numbers read from the screen or an API
Compute a complex condition then branch on the result
avoid: Taking a number from text like “1,234,000 đ” → use a text-processing node first, then Calculate
tips: Decimals use a dot.
Branch on the result: [[node:if]] comparing {{nX.output.value}} with true.

open.tech: Opens a URL in the operating system's default browser, or opens a file / application with its associated program (macOS: open; Windows: ShellExecute). The URL accepts {{variables}}.
open.accuracy: It only opens – it does not know whether the page has finished loading, and it does not read the page content.
open.speed: Almost instant; the page / app shows a few hundred ms to a few seconds later.
good: The start of a script: open a page, an Excel file, an application
A page needing an account already signed in on normal Chrome
avoid: A page for the Web nodes to control → [[node:openWeb]] (the app's own Chrome)
Changing the page in an existing tab → [[node:browserGo]]
tips: After an Open node add a Wait node (image / text / [[node:waitScreen]]) before clicking.
The window just opened (or the window of an already-open app) is brought to the front – later type / click nodes go to the right app.
To be able to close this tab later: connect [[node:browserTab]] by the tab the Open node opened.
fields: **Browser** – choose the browser when opening a URL

openWeb.tech: Starts the app's own Chrome (or Edge / Brave) with its own profile and a DevTools control port (CDP); the Web nodes talk to the page through that port, so they read the HTML directly and do not look at the screen.
openWeb.accuracy: Very high: finds elements by text / label / CSS instead of pixels. Pages that block bots, captchas or canvas cannot be read – use the *Test page* button.
openWeb.speed: Opening the browser takes a few seconds the first time; later runs reuse the open window.
good: Public web pages, forms, tables, feeds
Background running: a covered / minimised window keeps running
avoid: A page needing an account signed in on normal Chrome → [[node:clickElement]] (Accessibility) or sign in once in the app's Chrome
Games / canvas → [[node:clickImage]]
tips: The app's profile keeps your sign-in between runs: signing in by hand once is enough.
Click the globe *Test page* button before writing the script to learn whether the page is blocked.
With Wisp: [[chapter:settings-browser]] choose Wisp (or Automatic when Wisp is open) – the web nodes run on Wisp and do not take over the mouse.
fields: **Wait for load** – wait until the page settles before continuing

window.tech: Lists and controls windows through the OS API (macOS: Accessibility + CoreGraphics; Windows: Win32). Finds a window by app name and title.
window.accuracy: Exact when the app name / title is right. Frames are set by presets computed from each display's work area.
window.speed: Instant; *wait for open / close* lasts until the window appears or the time runs out.
good: The start of a script: bring the window to the front and set its position + size so coordinates / template images do not drift
Wait for a dialog window to open or close
avoid: Only need to know whether an app is running → [[node:app]]
A window inside a web page → the web nodes
tips: Set the size with a preset (left half, right half, centre…) then click using coordinates anchored to the window.
The overlay draws the target frame so you can preview where the window will sit.
fields: **Action** – bring to front / wait for open / wait for close / set frame / minimise / close
**Window** – choose from the open list or type the app name + title

app.tech: Asks the OS for the list of application processes; quitting uses a polite close request, while *force quit* ends the process. System apps are blocked.
app.accuracy: By application name / id – it does not look at the screen.
app.speed: Instant; waiting to open / quit lasts until the state changes or the time runs out.
good: Check whether an app is running then branch (Yes / No ports)
Quit the app at the end of a script
avoid: Need to operate inside a window → [[node:window]]
Look at a process's CPU / RAM → [[node:process]]
tips: To open an app: an [[node:open]] node, then an App node set to *wait for running*.
*Force quit* and *close window* are dangerous actions – the app asks for confirmation per script.
fields: **Action** – check / wait for running / wait for quit / quit / force quit

browserTab.tech: Controls the tabs of the Chrome / Edge / Brave / Cốc Cốc you use every day: macOS through JXA `osascript`, Windows through UI Automation. It closes exactly the tab an Open node opened, by tab id.
browserTab.accuracy: By tab URL / title. Needs Automation permission for the browser (macOS).
browserTab.speed: A few tens to a few hundred ms per command.
good: Read the URL / title of the tab you are viewing then branch
Clean up tabs after a run: close the tab an Open node opened
avoid: Controlling page content through the DOM → [[node:openWeb]] + web nodes
Changing the page in a tab → [[node:browserGo]]
tips: List the tabs into the output then [[node:forEach]] over each tab.
An Open node remembers its tab when a Tab node points at it.
fields: **Action** – read / list / switch / open / close / reload / wait
**Browser** and **tab** – by URL, title, id or Open node

browserGo.tech: Changes the current tab's address through AppleScript (macOS) / UI Automation (Windows) then waits for the tab to report it has loaded.
browserGo.accuracy: Reliable for changing the page; the load wait follows the browser's state, not the content.
browserGo.speed: As fast as the page loads.
good: Visit several pages in turn in the same tab, with URLs built from variables
Want to keep normal Chrome's sign-in
avoid: Opening a new tab → [[node:open]]
A page that needs DOM reading → [[node:openWeb]]
tips: After this node connect [[node:pageText]] or [[node:readTable]] to read the page that just loaded.
fields: **Wait for load** – up to how long

browserNorm.tech: Sets a standard state for the browser window: leaves full screen, sets the window size, resets zoom to 100 %, closes small popups.
browserNorm.accuracy: Keeps coordinates and template images from drifting between runs.
good: Right after an Open node, before clicking by coordinates / image / text
avoid: Not needed if you already use web nodes or Accessibility elements (independent of window size)
tips: Use the same size as when the template image was captured.
When window sizing is on you must choose the target: the Open node's tab, or the browser + tab by title / URL – so it does not resize the wrong window you are using.

savePdf.tech: Sends Cmd+P (Windows: Ctrl+P) to Chrome / Edge, clicks the print dialog's Save button (read through Accessibility / UI Automation), types the path into the save-file dialog, then waits for the file to be written.
savePdf.accuracy: Depends on the browser's print dialog: the print destination must be *Save as PDF*.
good: Save invoices, reports, signed-in pages as PDF
avoid: A non-Chromium browser (Firefox, Safari)
Need the page's text → [[node:pageText]]
tips: The file name accepts {{variables}}; an existing file of the same name is overwritten.
The result goes in the output `path`.

elementAction.tech: Calls the element's own action directly through the Accessibility tree (macOS AX / Windows UIA): click, fill a value, tick, select – without the real mouse.
elementAction.accuracy: High when the element has a clear name / role; a custom field may not accept the value – use [[node:type]].
elementAction.speed: Fast (reads the tree once, then calls).
good: Fill forms, tick boxes without grabbing the mouse
A covered window still works
avoid: An element that only accepts the real mouse → [[node:clickElement]]
A public web page → [[node:webType]]
tips: Use *Pick on screen* and *Try find* in the inspector to get the right query.
fields: **Find by** – text / label / role + Nth occurrence

elementRead.tech: Finds an element in the Accessibility tree then reads its text / value (no OCR); optionally reads the text next to a label.
elementRead.accuracy: Verbatim text – more exact than OCR; it cannot read where the app does not expose its element tree.
good: Get a price, a balance on a signed-in page in normal Chrome
Read an input box in an app
avoid: A web page in the app's Chrome → [[node:webRead]]
A screen with no tree (game, remote) → [[node:waitText]]
tips: Reading text next to a label: choose the label then take the adjacent value.
Connect [[node:textNumber]] to extract a number.
fields: **Read** – text / value / next to a label

readTable.tech: Reads a table / grid through the Accessibility tree into rows + columns; optionally writes .csv / .xlsx.
readTable.accuracy: Exact to the cell content; a virtualised table (only the visible part is drawn) can only be read where visible.
readTable.speed: Fast; a long table depends on the number of cells.
good: Get an order table / price table then [[node:forEach]] each row
Save a table as an Excel file
avoid: A table in the app's Chrome → [[node:webRead]]
tips: The outputs `rows` / `items` / `columns` can be used right away in later nodes.

readDocument.tech: Reads the content of an edit box / document through Accessibility (Windows: UI Automation – Word / Notepad through TextPattern), keeping line breaks; or only the selected part.
good: Get a note in TextEdit / Notepad / Word then split into lines
avoid: A web page → [[node:pageText]]
tips: Select a passage by hand or with Cmd/Ctrl+A, then turn on *selected part only*.

pageText.tech: Walks the Accessibility tree of a window / one frame and gathers all visible text.
good: Get a whole page / a list on a signed-in page then split into lines
avoid: Need the text of one spot → [[node:elementRead]]
tips: Connect [[node:textSplit]] / [[node:textMatch]] to extract data.
fields: **Scope** – the whole window or one frame

waitUIEvent.tech: Re-reads the Accessibility tree every 200 ms to detect a new window, a change of the topmost window, a new element or a changed value.
waitUIEvent.accuracy: More reliable than waiting for an image: independent of the look.
good: A button that opens a slow-to-appear dialog
Wait for an app to open a new window
avoid: Waiting by text / image on screen → [[node:waitText]], [[node:waitImage]]
tips: Set the wait time just long enough to report errors early.

waitDownload.tech: Scans the downloads folder for a new file matching the name pattern, waits until the temporary suffix (.crdownload, .part) is gone and the size stops changing.
waitDownload.accuracy: Very reliable for files downloaded by a browser.
good: After a Download / Export file button on the web, then open or read the file
avoid: Calling a file-download API directly → [[node:http]]
tips: The outputs `path` / `name` / `size` are used by the file / zip nodes.

webWait.tech: Runs through the app's Chrome (CDP): finds an element in the HTML, including same-origin iframes, then acts with browser events; a covered window still works.
webWait.accuracy: Very high: by text / label / CSS, independent of pixels or theme.
webWait.speed: Faster than waiting for an image; it waits for the frame to be still before concluding.
good: Wait for the page to load, wait for search results
Wait for an element to disappear (a spinner)
avoid: A bot-blocking page / canvas → [[node:waitImage]]
tips: Try a selector with *Try find*, get one with *Pick element on page*.
A label with a changing part ("Messenger, 1 unread", "Inbox (3)") → write only the fixed part, no double quotes: aria=Messenger. Pasting aria-label=… from DevTools also works.

A page that opens an alert / confirm / prompt box: by default the node fails at once with `web_dialog` carrying the box text; to continue, set **JS dialog** (webDialog) *Click OK* / *Click Cancel* – the box text is in the output `dialogText`.
fields: **Find by** – text / aria / role / label / css / xpath
**Scope** – the whole page or a dialog

webClick.tech: Runs through the app's Chrome (CDP): finds an element in the HTML, including same-origin iframes, then acts with browser events; a covered window still works.
webClick.accuracy: Very high: by text / label / CSS, independent of pixels or theme.
webClick.speed: Fast; it tries hovering before clicking to be sure of hitting the element.
good: A page whose layout / theme changes often and breaks template images
Click a button inside a dialog (*dialog* scope)
avoid: A page needing normal sign-in → [[node:clickElement]]
tips: After clicking, the node waits for the page to settle (up to 3 s) before continuing; outputs `navigated` (moved to another page / URL changed), `url`, `popup` (URL of a newly opened tab) – connect [[node:if]] to branch when a click does not change the page.
Several elements with the same text: set *Nth occurrence* or limit it to a dialog.

A page that opens an alert / confirm / prompt box: by default the node fails at once with `web_dialog` carrying the box text; to continue, set **JS dialog** (webDialog) *Click OK* / *Click Cancel* – the box text is in the output `dialogText`.

webType.tech: Runs through the app's Chrome (CDP): finds an element in the HTML, including same-origin iframes, then acts with browser events; a covered window still works.
webType.accuracy: Very high: by text / label / CSS, independent of pixels or theme.
webType.speed: Fast; typing goes through browser events.
good: Fill forms, search boxes, comments
avoid: An app outside the browser → [[node:type]] or [[node:elementAction]]
tips: After typing, the node waits for the page to settle like [[node:webClick]]; outputs `navigated`, `url`, `popup` (e.g. Enter submitting the form to another page).
Turn on clearing the old text before typing.
A hard-to-fill field: try [[node:webKey]].

A page that opens an alert / confirm / prompt box: by default the node fails at once with `web_dialog` carrying the box text; to continue, set **JS dialog** (webDialog) *Click OK* / *Click Cancel* – the box text is in the output `dialogText`.

webRead.tech: Runs through the app's Chrome (CDP): finds an element in the HTML, including same-origin iframes, then acts with browser events; a covered window still works.
webRead.accuracy: Very high: by text / label / CSS, independent of pixels or theme.
good: Get a price, an order code, a balance, a link into a variable
avoid: Text in an app outside the browser → [[node:elementRead]]
tips: Read attributes such as href, src, value.
Connect [[node:textNumber]] to extract a number.

A page that opens an alert / confirm / prompt box: by default the node fails at once with `web_dialog` carrying the box text; to continue, set **JS dialog** (webDialog) *Click OK* / *Click Cancel* – the box text is in the output `dialogText`.

webKey.tech: Sends keys into the app's Chrome tab through CDP – the browser need not be in front and the real keyboard is not touched.
webKey.accuracy: Reliable: the key lands on the right page.
good: Esc to close a dialog, Tab to the next field, Enter to submit a form
avoid: OS shortcuts → [[node:key]]
tips: Use it when clicking a button does nothing but Enter works.
After pressing, it waits for the page to settle like [[node:webClick]]; outputs `navigated`, `url`, `popup`.

webScroll.tech: Runs through the app's Chrome (CDP): finds an element in the HTML, including same-origin iframes, then acts with browser events; a covered window still works.
webScroll.accuracy: Very high: by text / label / CSS, independent of pixels or theme.
good: Bring a button at the bottom of the page into view
Scroll a feed until an element appears
avoid: Scrolling an app outside the browser → [[node:scroll]]
tips: Scrolling inside its own frame: choose that frame instead of scrolling the whole page.

A page that opens an alert / confirm / prompt box: by default the node fails at once with `web_dialog` carrying the box text; to continue, set **JS dialog** (webDialog) *Click OK* / *Click Cancel* – the box text is in the output `dialogText`.
fields: **Scroll type** – to an element / inside a frame / until seen

screenshot.tech: Captures the screen through the OS API (macOS needs Screen Recording permission), crops to the area and saves a PNG; it can also copy to the clipboard.
screenshot.speed: A few tens to a few hundred ms.
good: Save evidence after placing an order / transferring money
Capture a result to send on through [[node:http]] or [[node:clipboard]]
avoid: Only need text on screen → [[node:waitText]] (no image to save)
Capturing a background web tab → the AI uses the `screenshot` tool
tips: The output `path` is for later nodes; files never overwrite each other.
Change the image folder in Settings → Storage.
fields: **Area** – script region / whole screen / fixed / where the previous node found something

clipboard.tech: Reads / writes the operating system clipboard (text or a PNG image).
clipboard.accuracy: Verbatim; an image is written from a file.
good: Copy / paste a large amount of text faster than typing key by key
Copy an image just captured to paste into a chat
avoid: Typing a little text → [[node:type]] (does not touch your clipboard)
tips: Combine with [[node:key]] Cmd/Ctrl+C and Cmd/Ctrl+V.
It overwrites the current clipboard – do not use it while you are copying by hand.
fields: **Action** – read text / write text / write image

http.tech: Makes HTTP calls from your machine (GET / POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE) with parameters, headers, a JSON / form body; reads JSON into the output.
http.accuracy: As per the server's response; the status code is in the output.
http.speed: Depends on the network and server.
good: Fetch data / send an order / report results to Telegram, a webhook
Call an API instead of operating the UI
avoid: An API needing a complicated browser sign-in → act on the page with web nodes
tips: Keep API keys in Settings → Secrets and call `{{secret.<name>}}` – the value is masked in results.
Read nested JSON fields with a path in the output.

file.tech: File operations through the operating system: write text, append a .csv / .xlsx row, create a folder, delete to the Trash, empty the Trash.
file.accuracy: Exact; deleting always goes to the Trash (recoverable) unless you choose empty the Trash.
good: Write each loop's log / result to Excel
Clean up old screenshots
avoid: Reading a table from a page → [[node:readTable]]
tips: Delete and empty the Trash are dangerous actions – the app asks for confirmation.
The file name accepts {{variables}}.
fields: **Action** – write / append row / create folder / delete / empty

system.tech: Adjusts the speaker volume through the operating system's audio API.
good: Turn music to a comfortable level, mute before a meeting
avoid: Changing the speaker / microphone, playing an alert sound → [[node:display]]
tips: Read the current level so you can restore it at the end of the script.
fields: **Action** – set level / raise / lower / mute / unmute

display.tech: Controls the OS display / audio: light / dark mode, brightness, the default speaker / microphone device, playing an alert sound; or reads the state.
display.accuracy: As per the OS API; some machines do not allow changing brightness.
good: Switch to headphones before a call
Play a sound when done
avoid: Only adjusting the volume → [[node:system]]
Showing a text notification → [[node:notify]]
tips: Read the state then branch with [[node:if]].
fields: **Action** – dark mode / brightness / audio device / alert sound / read

power.tech: Calls the operating system's power commands: lock the screen, turn off the display, sleep, log out, shut down, restart; or keep the machine awake while running.
power.accuracy: Certain, but an action that ends the session needs your consent and has a countdown so you can cancel.
good: Shut down when a long overnight job finishes
Keep the machine from sleeping during a long run
avoid: Only want to say it is done → [[node:notify]]
tips: Put the power node at the end, after everything that needs the machine on.
The countdown gives you time to press Cancel.

notify.tech: Shows an operating system notification (macOS Notification Center, Windows toast) with a title + content.
notify.accuracy: Shows text only, no buttons yet.
good: Say the script is done / needs attention while the app is minimised
avoid: Remote notification → [[node:http]] calling Telegram / a webhook
Need a person to press Approve / Deny midway → [[node:askUser]]
tips: The title and content accept {{variables}}.

askUser.tech: Pauses the flow; the mini bar expands into a question card (question, list of items, optional input box, Approve / Deny buttons) with a system notification; when on the main screen a dialog appears in the middle.
askUser.accuracy: Certain – it continues only when you click, and on timeout it takes the Timed out port.
askUser.speed: Waits until you answer (Wait up to; 0 = wait forever).
good: Approve beforehand work that is hard to undo: sending messages / emails, deleting, paying
Enter a code only you know midway (OTP, captcha) in the input box
avoid: Scheduled / CLI / API runs with nobody at the machine – the node goes straight out the Timed out port
Only need to inform, no answer needed → [[node:notify]]
A value known when you press Run → a script input
tips: The question and the item list accept {{variables}} – e.g. a list of emails read by an earlier node, one item per line.
Text typed in the input box is in the output text, e.g. {{n3.output.text}}.
While an AI runs: the AI only sees the question (needs_input) and reminds you – it does not answer for you.
Touching the mouse to answer does not pause the script.

zip.tech: Compresses a folder / files into a .zip by a name pattern, or extracts a .zip; extraction blocks zip slip (it never writes outside the target folder).
good: Package results before sending
Open a package that was just downloaded ([[node:waitDownload]])
avoid: Only need to copy a file → [[node:shell]]
tips: The name pattern accepts {{variables}}, e.g. a date-time from [[node:textNumber]].

inputSource.tech: Reads / changes the operating system's input method (macOS Input Source, Windows layout); warns when Unikey / EVKey is running.
inputSource.accuracy: As per the OS; Unikey / EVKey type accents themselves so they are only reported, not controllable.
good: Set ABC before typing so accents are not garbled
Branch by the input method in use
avoid: Turning Vietnamese typing on / off with the typing app's shortcut → the [[node:key]] node
tips: Place it right before [[node:type]].

process.tech: Reads a process's CPU / RAM through the OS API; lists, waits for it to run / quit / become idle.
process.accuracy: A measurement at the moment of reading; CPU is sampled over a short interval.
good: Wait for a render / export to finish
Stop when an app uses too much RAM
avoid: Only need to know whether an app is running → [[node:app]]
tips: Wait for *idle* instead of a fixed wait.
fields: **Action** – read / list / wait for running / wait for quit / wait for idle

sysInfo.tech: Reads the battery, CPU / RAM, free disk, display, network and machine name once.
good: Stop when the battery is low, warn when the disk is nearly full, wait when the network is lost
avoid: Watching a single process → [[node:process]]
tips: Connect [[node:if]] or [[node:calc]] to compare with a threshold.
fields: **Output** battery / cpu / ram / disk / network / machine name

osShortcut.tech: Runs a Shortcut in macOS's Shortcuts app, passing text in and taking text back. macOS only.
osShortcut.accuracy: As per the Shortcut you created.
good: Reuse work already built as a Shortcut
avoid: Windows → [[node:shell]]
tips: Try the Shortcut in the Shortcuts app first.

shell.tech: Runs a command through the shell / PowerShell / AppleScript, taking the printed text and exit code.
shell.accuracy: As per the command; a non-zero exit code is reported as an error.
good: Work with no dedicated node yet, batch renaming, calling command-line tools
avoid: If a dedicated node does that job (files, zip, process) use that node
tips: Each command content must be approved by you – changing the command asks again. A command that only calls a script file (`sh x.sh`, `python3 y.py`) also asks again if the file's content changes.
The printed text goes to the output for further filtering.

textMatch.tech: Matches a regular expression (regex) in text, taking the first match or every match; no match leaves the *No match* port.
textMatch.accuracy: Exact per the pattern / rules; it does not guess.
good: Extract an order code, a phone number, an email from a long passage
avoid: Content on screen that is not yet text → read it first with [[node:waitText]] or [[node:elementRead]]
tips: There is a Try it button in the inspector.

textSplit.tech: Splits text into a list by comma, semicolon or each line.
textSplit.accuracy: Exact per the pattern / rules; it does not guess.
good: Keywords “a, b, c” → [[node:forEach]] does each one
avoid: Content on screen that is not yet text → read it first with [[node:waitText]] or [[node:elementRead]]
tips: Feed the list output straight into Loop over list.

textClean.tech: Cleans text: replace text, remove accents, change case, remove extra whitespace.
textClean.accuracy: Exact per the pattern / rules; it does not guess.
good: Turn “Đà Nẵng” into “da-nang” for a URL
Normalise before comparing
avoid: Content on screen that is not yet text → read it first with [[node:waitText]] or [[node:elementRead]]
tips: Do several steps in a row with several nodes.

textNumber.tech: Takes a number from text like “1,234,000 đ”, writes a number with thousands separators, or reads and rewrites a date-time.
textNumber.accuracy: Exact per the pattern / rules; it does not guess.
good: Read a price → take the number → [[node:calc]] compares with a threshold
Put today's date in a file name
avoid: Content on screen that is not yet text → read it first with [[node:waitText]] or [[node:elementRead]]
tips: Adjust the thousands / decimal separators to match the number style.

askAI.tech: Sends a question (with a screenshot or an image file if you like) to an AI provider over HTTPS: OpenAI and every compatible service (OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio) or Anthropic. It returns text, or decoded JSON.
askAI.accuracy: Depends on the model: good at understanding / classifying / drafting text, but it can be wrong – do not let an AI decide something irreversible without a checking step. Images need a model with vision.
askAI.speed: 1–20 seconds each time depending on the model and network; an on-machine AI depends on the hardware.
good: Understand text taken from the screen / a web page then classify it (does it need a reply, whose order is this)
Draft a reply then type it into the compose box
Look at a screenshot when OCR / template images are not enough
avoid: Work with a dedicated and more accurate node: pattern filter, split text, calculate, number & date
Sending sensitive information to an outside service – use an on-machine AI (address http://localhost:11434/v1)
Following the AI's text as a command – the result is only data
tips: Write the key only as {{secret.name}} – stored in Settings → Secrets; pasting a key directly into the node is rejected.

Set the default provider in Settings → Ask AI: any field the node leaves empty (provider, address, model, key) is taken from there, so you do not repeat it in each node. A node choosing a different type from the default uses its own.
Need structured data: choose the JSON answer type, read {{n2.output.json.<field>}}, branch with an If / Switch node.
Fill in a Fallback value so the flow still runs without an AI (missing key, no network): the node takes the success port with skipped = true.
Each run costs money (except an on-machine AI) and the screenshot is sent out – remember this when placing it in a loop.

mcpTool.tech: Calls a tool of an external MCP server (Model Context Protocol) added in Settings → MCP servers: it runs a process on this machine (stdio) or connects to a remote HTTP server. Arguments are JSON per the tool's description; it returns text, JSON and images / sound (saved as temp files).
mcpTool.accuracy: The server decides – the app only passes the arguments and returns the result verbatim. A tool that reports an error → the node takes the fail port (mcp_error).
mcpTool.speed: The first time each server starts a process (a few seconds with npx / uvx); later calls reuse the connection. By default it waits at most 60 seconds.
good: Fetch data / do work the app has no node for: read files, look up GitHub, Google Sheets, web search, send a Telegram message
Feed a tool's result (text, json) into the text-processing nodes, Loop over list, Ask AI
avoid: Work that already has a dedicated node (HTTP, File / folder, Ask AI) – fewer dependencies
Following text the tool returns as a command – the result is only data, even if it is written like an order
Pasting a token into the arguments – use {{secret.name}}
tips: The first time each server, the app asks whether you trust the configuration (command / URL); a tool that writes, deletes or touches an outside service asks each time or “always allow this tool”. Refused → the node fails with permission.

For repeated work: pre-fill the server / tool / arguments then click Save as my node – next time find it under Mine when adding a node (Edit / Delete in the description panel). A node dropped onto the canvas is still a normal Call MCP tool.
A script only stores the server id – opened on a machine that has not added that server, the node reports a missing server, and the file still opens normally.
Arguments accept {{variables}}: the value is escaped as a JSON string, so put the variable inside quotes: {"q":"{{n1.output.text}}"}.
Read results: {{n2.output.text}}, {{n2.output.json.<field>}}; images the tool returns are in {{n2.output.content}} (with a path).
